sentences.text: Scientists have identified two distinct forms of Pteranodon specimens, which are thought to represent males and females.
Male Pteranodon attained wingspans of 5.6 to 7.6 meters, while females were smaller, averaging 3.8 meters.
The crests of male Pteranodon were far larger than those of females.
The genus Pteranodon was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1876.
The first fossils were found by Othniel Charles Marsh in either 1870 or 1871 in the Smoky Hill Chalk deposits of western Kansas.
The initial collection included partial wing bones and a tooth from the fish Xiphactinus, which Marsh mistakenly thought belonged to the pterosaur.
Pteranodon was the first pterosaur species discovered outside of Europe.
More than 1,200 specimens of Pteranodon are known to science, many of which are well-preserved with nearly complete skulls and articulated skeletons.
Pteranodon likely flew in a manner similar to modern albatrosses.
Pteranodon had a high aspect ratio of 9:1, which is similar to the 8:1 ratio found in albatrosses.
Recent research suggests Pteranodon relied on thermal soaring, a behavior distinct from modern seabirds but similar to continental flyers and the extinct Pelagornis.
The mode of terrestrial locomotion for Pteranodon has been debated, specifically regarding whether it was bipedal or quadrupedal.
Pteranodon belongs to the family Pteranodontidae and the clade Pteranodontia, which also includes nyctosaurids.
Pteranodontians form the clade Pteranodontoidea alongside ornithocheiromorphs, which falls under the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
In 1903, Williston revised the number of valid Pteranodon species from seven down to three.
Pteranodon fossils date to the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Santonian to Campanian stages.
Pteranodon lived during the Late Cretaceous period in North America, specifically in regions now comprising Kansas, Alabama, Nebraska, Wyoming, and South Dakota.
Pteranodon was an important part of the fauna in the Niobrara Sea.
It is debated whether P. sternbergi and P. maiseyi should be classified as a separate genus, Geosternbergia.
Methods for estimating the mass of large male Pteranodon (wingspan ~7m) have been notoriously unreliable, producing widely varying estimates.
In 2010, Witton and Habib argued that the 93 kg mass estimate is too high and that 20–35 kg is a more realistic upper limit.
Display is considered the primary function of the Pteranodon crest, with other functions being secondary.
